stemMd: A thermally insulated container is stirred vigorously with a paddle. No heat crosses its boundary. Can its internal energy increase?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Yes, because mechanical work can transfer energy into it.

options.label: C
options.textMd: No, because energy can enter only as heat.

options.label: D
options.textMd: No, because insulation prevents every form of energy transfer.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Yes, but only if its mass doubles.

explanationMd: An adiabatic boundary excludes heat transfer but not work. Stirring does work on the fluid, which can increase its internal energy and temperature. The first law tracks both channels of energy transfer.

distractorRationale.c: The first law includes work as well as heat.
distractorRationale.d: Thermal insulation prevents heat transfer, not necessarily shaft work.
distractorRationale.e: Work input can increase internal energy without mass change.
distractorRationale.b: The increase is consistent with energy conservation through work.
